What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson
Liverpool in late 2026 feature three £100m-plus signings. Each of them enjoyed among their best moments yet at Anfield. Florian Wirtz appeared refreshed by working over the international break with Jürgen Klopp, clearly still a scouse whisperer. Wirtz scored an improvised goal and set up another among 10 chances he created. Alexander Isak exposing Matthijs de Ligt and Leny Yoro for the latter’s dismissal was the moment to break the dam. If Bradley Barcola showed that finishing might not be his forte, his assist for Rio Ngumoha’s goal evidenced there is composure to accompany lightning speed. Ngumoha showed he has the talent to fetch a similar price tag, scoring and assisting at 18 years and 85 days, the youngest Liverpool player to do so since Michael Owen versus Leeds in December 1997. If Manchester United’s performance, and Mauricio Pochettino’s bizarre selection of De Ligt, opened the door, Liverpool stormed through it. Beating United never gets old, no matter their desiccated state. John Brewin
It has been a long time between drinks for Hull when it comes to Premier League wins: three months, in fact. Perhaps that is why the celebrations were so extreme after their win over Brighton on Sunday – though the manner of it, two injury-time goals after absorbing so much pressure all afternoon, will have contributed too. It was a much-needed victory for Hull, who continue to show signs they are perhaps the best equipped of the three promoted teams to survive. The gap to the relegation zome is now five points and their win underlined why the Tigers have the two real ingredients needed to survive. Konstantinos Tzolakis produced the goalkeeping display of the Premier League season to deny Brighton time and time again, while Oli McBurnie’s late double exemplified the kind of goal-poaching Hull will need if they are to beat the drop. Keep those two areas thriving, and Hull can perhaps look upwards, rather than over their shoulders. Aaron Bower
When Yasir al-Rumayyan, over from Riyadh to watch Matthias Jaissle’s team live for the first time this season, studied his team sheet, Newcastle’s chair presumably read between the lines. There was no space for Bazoumana Touré or Aladji Bamba (who cost a combined £78.5m) on a substitutes’ bench that in Nico González and Matias Fernandez-Pardo featured more than £100m worth of summer signings. Meanwhile, Amar Dedic and Sean Steur (a joint £50m outlay) were withdrawn at half-time and replaced by two members of Newcastle’s old guard, Tino Livramento and Jacob Ramsey. They played key roles in a renascent second half performance, with Jaissle’s revitalised team overcoming a 1-0 deficit to draw 2-2 against table-topping Arsenal. Afterwards Jaissle and al-Rumayyan chatted. “The chair analysed the game the way I did,” he said. “He knows about football.” Newcastle’s manager wants an increased say in a recruitment process currently controlled by sporting director Ross Wilson. Significantly, the goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek was the sole summer buy to feature in the second half. Over to you, Yasir. Louise Taylor
Chelsea’s injury list was no excuse for their performance in their 4-1 defeat by Leeds. They have spent more than £1bn putting this squad together and still had an £117m attacking midfielder, Morgan Rogers, in the starting XI. Leeds, by contrast, have had to be smarter with their budget and Daniel Farke has revitalised players who previously looked unlikely to flourish in the Premier League. Ethan Ampadu had to drop down a level after leaving Chelsea, while Jayden Bogle was relegated with Sheffield United five years ago. James Justin suffered a serious achilles injury not long after making his England debut in 2022 and Dominic Calvert-Lewin was close to being written off after leaving Everton in 2025. Yet Farke has found ways to improve these players. They are not fashionable names and did not cost much, but they are being coached well and are in a team with an identity. There is none of that at Chelsea. Jacob Steinberg
Enzo Maresca is still in the experimentation stage as Manchester City manager. Maybe the seven straight Premier League wins to start was a false indication of where the team are, in terms of progression in the post-Pep Guardiola era. It’s inevitable that a team will dip once the early adrenaline wears off and Maresca is finding this out. To rectify his team’s slow play and lack of energy, the all-action Elliot Anderson was pushed further forward to provide the thrust from the middle of the park, while his teammates were pedestrian. Ayyoub Bouaddi was given the responsibility of sitting, with Enzo Fernández left out. “We are trying to find different solutions, right balance, and to be more consistent,” Maresca said. It looks difficult to fit all three into the team and Maresca is yet to find the right answer after four games without a win, leaving the manager to return to the lab. Will Unwin
Frank Lampard said he had expected Thomas Frank to field a back three and that the realisation Crystal Palace would play a back four had prompted a hasty rejig. “I felt we needed a formation change and a little bit different players in different positions,” Frank said. “Getting some of the better players central, so I think in many spells it was very good. The main bit was the defensive side we need to keep working on and adjust.” But Palace are a team that have played with a back three for more than two seasons, and their squad is set up to play that way. If a back four is Frank’s vision, there will need to be some reprogramming; in the first half, as Frank admitted, there were times when both full-backs, Anan Khalaili and Tyrick Mitchell, pushed high and left them exposed, particularly given the lack of a natural defensive midfielder. The second half offered hope Frank’s changes can come good, but there is work to be done. Jonathan Wilson
James Maddison has backed Luca Williams-Barnett to take his spectacular full debut in his stride after helping the 18-year-old prepare for the game against Ipswich. Roberto De Zerbi revealed that Maddison played an important role in the buildup after deciding over the international break that he would give the England Under-19s forward the opportunity he has been craving. The Tottenham manager’s decision paid off handsomely as Williams-Barnett scored the opener before setting up Dominic Solanke for the second goal, with De Zerbi even comparing him to Lamine Yamal after the game. “It’s not always easy,” said Maddison when asked whether it would be difficult for Williams-Barnett to keep his feet on the ground. “He’ll have a lot of people in his ear, and it’s just about making sure he doesn’t get carried away with the praise he’s going to get. But he deserves it. He is someone who has big self-belief and confidence, so he doesn’t need to be held back. We’ve got a group of lads that I don’t think would let him get too big for his boots.” Ed Aarons
There was no greater endorsement of Jules Ahoka’s full Premier League debut than the words of Thomas Meunier, who knows what an elite player looks like. The 35-year-old Belgium defender counts Kylian Mbappé, Erling Haaland, Jude Bellingham and Kevin De Bruyne as former teammates, but another sprung to mind on Saturday afternoon after Ahoka helped win the midfield battle at Villa Park. “Jules, incredible … six months ago he was playing in Belgium for [Royal] Antwerp and now playing like Busquets,” Meunier said. The rangy 20-year-old, who again ably deputised for Granit Xhaka, was composed in possession and quick to eliminate danger. He made 16 defensive contributions in the game – attempted tackles, blocks, clearances and interceptions – more than any other player. Ahoka began last season playing on sandy pitches in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s second division for AC Normands but already looks at home at the top level. Ben Fisher
Bournemouth beating Nottingham Forest for a ninth victory in succession in all competitions speaks to the continued accomplishments of a recruitment policy that imports new faces into a settled structure. Adam Smith is a survivor from Eddie Howe’s promotion team of 2014-15. After the exile of Álex Jiménez for off-field reasons, Smith resumed at right-back to embody a club ethos that remains close to its roots despite the current rarefied status. Antonio Silva, the summer arrival who replaced Marcos Senesi, arrived into a settled defence alongside James Hill, Adrien Truffert and Smith. Only two goals have been conceded in that nine-game run, staging a platform from which attacking players are flourishing. Another week, another goal from Evanilson, in whom patience was placed under Andoni Iraola and now Marco Rose. “Evanilson creates space, carries the ball, provides assists and now he scores goals as a No 9,” said Rose. The bigger clubs trailing in Bournemouth’s wake have plenty to learn from them. John Brewin

המחזור האחרון בפרמייר ליג סיפק שורה של התפתחויות דרמטיות, בראשן פתיחת העונה הקשה של מנצ'סטר יונייטד תחת המאמן מאוריציו פוצ'טינו, שהובסה 4-0 באנפילד על ידי ליברפול לאחר כרטיס אדום מוקדם ללני יורו. מנגד, ליברפול המשיכה להציג יכולת מרשימה עם הופעות בולטות של פלוריאן וירץ והצעיר ריו נגומוה.

במקומות אחרים, האל סיטי רשמה ניצחון דרמטי על ברייטון הודות לשערים מאוחרים והצלה ענקית של השוער קונסטנטינוס צולאקיס, המרחקים אותה מהתחתית. ניוקאסל חילצה תיקו 2-2 מול ארסנל המובילה לאחר מחצית שנייה משופרת לעיני היושב-ראש יאסר א-רומאיאן, בעוד צ'לסי ספגה תבוסה 4-1 מול לידס המאורגנת של דניאל פארקה. במקביל, מנצ'סטר סיטי המשיכה לחפש פתרונות תחת אצו מארסקה לאחר רצף משחקים ללא ניצחון.
